title: vault-memory
gist: A memory layer for Claude over an Obsidian vault: each note is encoded once, and a question gets back one small block of memory instead of a grep session. I measured it against grep and search on questions checked against the notes.
summary: Gives a Claude session the answer from your notes in one small block, with the note each line came from.

hero_image.alt: Mean judged score against tokens into Claude on the SilverBullet docs: the recall agent sits just below the grep agent with fewer tokens, and single recall calls sit level with keyword search.

site.eyebrow: Agent memory · Obsidian · 89 public questions · MIT
site.blurb: Claude Code remembers by preloading an index and grepping a notes folder. vault-memory encodes each note once and answers a question with one small block. It beats search and comes within four questions of grep on the public docs with 26% fewer tokens, and the gap that is left is superseded facts.
